quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road.
questions.explanation: A cyclist may need to swerve suddenly to avoid objects on the road. They could move into traffic without warning. Always be very careful around bicyclists.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other slippery conditions. Winter driving is hard and requires extra care. Check antifreeze and washer fluid regularly. Snow tires give better grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may cross solid yellow lines only when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people in the crosswalk or crossing your path. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop. Yield to other traffic. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, check for another train on the other track.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check for another train on the other track.
questions.explanation: A second train may be coming on the other track. Wait until you are sure no train is approaching from either direction before crossing.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at incoming traffic.
Always stay at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid traffic jams.
Change lanes to make room for traffic to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to make room for traffic to enter.
questions.explanation: Make space for vehicles entering the road. If the lane next to you is empty, move over to let traffic in.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A no passing zone.
A one-way traffic area.
The blind spot of a large vehicle.
An area for motor vehicles only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around large trucks and vehicles. Stay out of these areas.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you with bright headlights. What should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from bright headlights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four lanes ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two-way traffic is coming.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the edge of the road marks the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder. When this line angles toward the center of the road, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
Reduce your following distance.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control on these surfaces.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road when parking downhill. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What do downward-pointing triangular signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You may proceed when the road is clear and it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following, except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left curve is ahead.
A series of curves is ahead.
An S-curve is ahead.
The road will be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will be slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is especially slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill, since oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By using the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or in curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not cross solid yellow lines to pass.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive as you would on dry roads.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery roads. Your vehicle will take longer to stop.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are difficult to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger vehicles.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are harder to spot than larger vehicles because they are smaller and have less noticeable lights. Stay alert to prevent collisions with these road users.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on an upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians can move out of your way.
Honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians crossing. You must stop before crossing the sidewalk area. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if it is safe.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
You cannot pass.
You can pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions can pass. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can safely move back into the right lane.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line mean?

options.text: You can pass, even if it is dangerous.
Traffic moves in opposite directions.
You cannot pass.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and go.
Stop, check all directions, then proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic signal, yield to vehicles approaching from the right. Always be ready to yield to prevent a crash. Take your foot off the gas, be ready to brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When driving past a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you approach.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a car that just parked, expect the driver to open the door as you approach. Use extra caution when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must stop within ____ of the first rail when told to stop.

options.text: 70 feet
50 feet
15 feet
5 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail when warning lights flash, gates lower, or you are told to stop.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you use?

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
Turn into the middle lane.
Turn into any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: If your car has an Anti-Lock Braking System and starts to slip on a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: If your car with an Anti-Lock Braking System starts to slip, press hard on the brake pedal and hold it while steering to safety. The ABS automatically pumps the brakes faster than you could. If you release pressure or pump the brakes yourself, you turn off the ABS.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It causes hearing loss.
It creates pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It causes poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system moves harmful gases out of your car and stops fumes from entering the passenger area. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the car and poison you. Fix any exhaust system leaks right away.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does a yellow X on a lane signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to turn to a green arrow.
The signal is about to turn to a red X.
Drivers may drive normally in this lane.
Drivers may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The signal is about to turn to a red X.
questions.explanation: Lane signals show which lanes are open or closed and change based on traffic flow. A yellow X means you should leave the lane immediately. The signal will soon change to a red X.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their bright headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their bright headlights, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You can no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Move slowly until traffic ahead clears.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive through completely.
Honk to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive through completely.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through it. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: If you must have higher insurance coverage but cannot prove it, what happens?

options.text: Your license and plates will be suspended for up to three years.
You can only drive on residential roads.
You will receive a warning.
Nothing will happen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license and plates will be suspended for up to three years.
questions.explanation: Higher insurance coverage is required for drivers convicted of a DUI, with too many points, or other serious violations. If you cannot prove you have this coverage, your license and plates may be suspended for up to three years.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs that show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your car will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is starting ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads. Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for hazards ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that a sharp turn is coming and you need to reduce your speed.

questions.question: Low beam headlights are effective at speeds up to how many mph?

options.text: 10 mph.
25 mph.
50 mph.
70 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights work well at speeds up to 25 mph. Do not drive faster than you can see within your headlights.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, what should you do?

options.text: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: Return to the right lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you just passed.

questions.question: The traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Consider it a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop immediately.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light appears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes conditions less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway where there are other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet, visibility is poor, or any other condition is not ideal. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are under the posted limit if conditions are poor.

questions.question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on limited-access highways?

options.text: 70 mph
55 mph
45 mph
30 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 70 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on limited-access highways is 70 mph. Follow posted signs if they show a different speed limit.
